thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected for gateway-US-WEST2. 10m error rate 5xx=14% (baseline 0.6%). Auto-escalation triggered. Runbook: https://runbook.internal/redwood/incidents/1793456789

sanjay (oncall): Acked. Investigating. I see 502/504 spikes on the LB -> gateway path.

elaine (sre): I'm pulling traces now. Initial look: request latency to model backends in us-west2 has increased and tcp retransmits spiked. Could be network flaps or host-level OOMs.

leo (platform): Checking infra metrics — nodepool us-west2-gpu-pool cpulimit and pod eviction events. Nothing yet for CPU, some EVict for memory on gateway-v2-*.

sanjay (oncall): Can we pin down whether this is a single AZ? I see region-level elevated error rate but not total loss.

elaine (sre): Zooming into AZs: us-west2-a is 80% of 5xx, us-west2-b is ok. So partial in us-west2-a.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: sanjay assigned. Handoff ETA 30m if no fix.

sanjay (oncall): Running quick mitigation: add temporary routing policy to shift 40% of traffic from us-west2-a -> us-east2 to reduce customer impact. Applying router policy now.

leo (platform): FYI: cross-region routing requires capacity check. us-east2 has spare capacity for this load but we may need to warm model KV caches. Recommend shifting lower qps first.

sanjay (oncall): Doing a gradual rollout via `rbctl`:
```
rbctl route modify --from region=us-west2-a --to region=us-east2 --pct=20
sleep 60
rbctl route modify --from region=us-west2-a --to region=us-east2 --pct=40
```

maya (oncall-2): I'll monitor error rate and tail latency while you shift traffic. Let me know when to ramp.

sanjay (oncall): Ramped to 20% -> metrics improving. Ramping to 40% now.

elaine (sre): 5xx in us-west2-a dropping to 6% overall. Customer visible errors reported by synthetic monitors also dropping. Good sign.

cs-rep (customer-success): We have a few customers flagged in our SLA dashboard showing elevated errors (org-RED-42, org-BLUE-9). I can notify them that we've shifted a portion of traffic and are investigating; ETA to full mitigation ~30-45m. Want approval to send a short note.

sanjay (oncall): Send the note. Keep it high level: affected region, mitigation (traffic shift to us-east2), monitoring, and we'll update in 30m or on resolution.

cs-rep (customer-success): Will do. Draft: "We're seeing increased 5xx responses from requests routed via us-west2 for some workloads. We have shifted traffic to an alternate region to reduce impact and are actively investigating. We'll follow up with updates."

leo (platform): While routing helps, we need root cause. I'm checking node logs in us-west2-a for OOM/killed pods. `kubectl get events -n gateway --field-selector involvedObject.name=gateway-v2-xyz` returned repeated `OOMKilled` entries around 17:12:03 UTC.

elaine (sre): Aha — memory pressure makes sense with a model / batch combo that recently rolled. Any recent deploys? eng-releases show a canary deployed to us-west2 yesterday for `gateway-v2` with increased default batch_size=1024.

sanjay (oncall): Rollback candidate: revert the canary config that raised batch size. That should reduce memory footprint per pod. Can someone confirm the canary id?

leo (platform): Canary tag `gateway-v2@2026-03-12-canary-37`. I can roll it back via the release manager `relman rollback gateway-v2 2026-03-11-stable` — but that is a config rollback not code. It will restart pods. Expect some churn.

maya (oncall-2): Rolling config rollback now in us-west2-a only (`relman rollback --region=us-west2-a gateway-v2 2026-03-11-stable`). Monitoring pod restarts.

incident-bot: Deploy job started: rollback-gateway-v2-1793456789. CI shows 8/10 pods restarting.

elaine (sre): Watch for connection drain; make sure we don't push more traffic back to dying pods. Keep cross-region shift until pods healthy.

sanjay (oncall): Agreed. Holding routing at 40% until health checks show `ready` for new pods.

maya (oncall-2): Rollback finished in us-west2-a. New pods are starting. Health probes are green on 6/8 and the remaining are spinning up.

leo (platform): Memory pressure dropping, OOM events ceased. Good.

elaine (sre): Observability: 5xx overall down to 1.2%. Latency tail returning to normal.

sanjay (oncall): Gradually shifting traffic back: `rbctl route modify --from region=us-west2-a --to region=us-east2 --pct=20` (i.e., reduce the diversion).

maya (oncall-2): Reduced to 20%. Watching metrics. No spike.

cs-rep (customer-success): Sent customers initial note and added that we expect to resume normal routing shortly.

sanjay (oncall): Reduced diversion to 0%. All traffic back to us-west2-a. Monitoring post-mitigation for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Postmortem required. Severity: Sev2 (partial outage, customer impact). Link to incident board: https://incidents.internal/redwood/1793456789

elaine (sre): I'll start the postmortem draft. Preliminary action items: revert risky canary configs to slower rollout, add automatic batch_size circuit breaker per-region, add pre-deploy memory-impact tests to the release pipeline.

sanjay (oncall): Handing off to maya for post-incident monitoring and follow-up. I'm going offline for 1hr.

maya (oncall-2): Taking follow-up. I'll complete the postmortem and coordinate with releases/eng-runtime on mitigations.

cs-rep (customer-success): I'll follow up with affected customers with summary once PMs approve.

sanjay (oncall): :white_check_mark: Thanks team.

incident-bot: This channel will be archived for the incident. If you need to reopen, reply `reopen 1793456789`.
